shared_elements: relief carving in low raised relief
glyph-like signs with rounded, cartouche-shaped outlines
dense rectilinear ordering of motifs into rows/columns or panels
elaborate scroll and volute infill within motif outlines
column of glyph blocks along one edge (B) matching the glyph grid of A
justification: Both surfaces carry the same distinctive repertoire of rounded, cartouche-framed glyph blocks packed with scrollwork and infill, and B carries a vertical column of such blocks that matches A's grid convention closely enough to suggest a shared sign system and carving style. The decisive difference is subject: A is entirely a grid of glyphs with no figure, while B is dominated by a large standing human figure in elaborate headdress holding an object, with glyphs merely subsidiary.
